import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Halperin conjecture

Suppose that $F \to E \to B$ is a fibration of simply connected spaces such that $F$ is
rationally elliptic and $\chi(F) \neq 0$ (i.e. $F$ has non-zero Euler characteristic). Then the
Serre spectral sequence associated to the fibration collapses at the $E_2$ page.

Here the Serre spectral sequence is the one for cohomology with rational coefficients. Its
collapse at $E_2$ is equivalent to the fibration being *totally non-cohomologous to zero* (TNCZ),
i.e. to the fibre inclusion $j \colon F \to E$ inducing a surjection
$j^* \colon H^*(E; \mathbb{Q}) \to H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$ (see [Lu97], §1). Since $\mathbb{Q}$ is a
field, $H^n(-; \mathbb{Q})$ is the linear dual of $H_n(-; \mathbb{Q})$, so this is in turn
equivalent to the injectivity of $j_* \colon H_*(F; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_*(E; \mathbb{Q})$ on rational
singular homology. This is the form in which the conjecture is stated below, using Mathlib's
singular homology `AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor`.

Following [Lu97], "fibration" means Serre fibration and all spaces are simply connected and of
finite rational type (finite-dimensional rational homology in each degree).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halperin_conjecture)
- [Lu97] G. Lupton, *Variations on a conjecture of Halperin*, Homotopy and Geometry
  (Warsaw, 1997), Banach Center Publ. 45 (1998), 115–135.
  [arXiv:math/0010124](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0010124)
-/

namespace HalperinConjecture

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicTopology Topology unitInterval
open scoped DirectSum TensorProduct

noncomputable section

/-- The `n`-th rational singular homology group $H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological
space `X`, as a `ℚ`-module. -/
abbrev rationalHomology (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) : ModuleCat ℚ :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).obj (TopCat.of X)

/-- The map $f_* \colon H_n(X; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(Y; \mathbb{Q})$ induced on rational singular
homology by a continuous map `f : X → Y`. -/
abbrev rationalHomologyMap {X Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : C(X, Y))
    (n : ℕ) : rationalHomology X n ⟶ rationalHomology Y n :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).map (TopCat.ofHom f)

/-- A topological space `X` is of *finite rational type* if each rational homology group
$H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ is finite-dimensional. -/
def IsFiniteRationalType (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∀ n, Module.Finite ℚ (rationalHomology X n)

/-- The (rational) *Euler characteristic*
$\chi(X) = \sum_n (-1)^n \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological space `X`.
This is the intended value when the total rational homology of `X` is finite-dimensional
(for instance when `X` is rationally elliptic); otherwise it is a junk value. -/
def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ n : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ n * Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology X n)

/-- A simply connected topological space `X` is *rationally elliptic* if both its total rational
homology $H_*(X; \mathbb{Q}) = \bigoplus_n H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ and its total rational homotopy
$\pi_*(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = \bigoplus_{n \ge 2} \pi_n(X, x) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ are
finite-dimensional. Only the homotopy groups $\pi_n$ with $n \ge 2$ are used since for a simply
connected space $\pi_1$ is trivial and $\pi_0$ is a point; the base point `x` is arbitrary since
`X` is path connected. -/
def IsRationallyElliptic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n, rationalHomology X n) ∧
    ∀ x : X, Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n, ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive (π_ (n + 2) X x))

/-- A continuous map `p : E → B` is a *Serre fibration* if it has the homotopy lifting property
with respect to all cubes $I^n$, $n \ge 0$: for every continuous `f : Iⁿ → E` and every homotopy
`H : I × Iⁿ → B` starting at `p ∘ f`, there is a homotopy `H' : I × Iⁿ → E` starting at `f` that
lifts `H`, i.e. `p ∘ H' = H`. -/
def IsSerreFibration {E B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] (p : C(E, B)) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : C(Fin n → I, E)) (H : C(I × (Fin n → I), B)), (∀ y, H (0, y) = p (f y)) →
    ∃ H' : C(I × (Fin n → I), E), (∀ y, H' (0, y) = f y) ∧ ∀ z, p (H' z) = H z

/-- The inclusion $j \colon F = p^{-1}(b) \to E$ of the fibre of `p : E → B` over `b : B`. -/
abbrev fibreInclusion {E B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] (p : C(E, B))
    (b : B) : C(p ⁻¹' {b}, E) :=
  ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩

/-- A rationally elliptic space is of finite rational type. -/
@[category API, AMS 55]
theorem IsRationallyElliptic.isFiniteRationalType {X : Type} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (hX : IsRationallyElliptic X) : IsFiniteRationalType X := fun n =>
  have := hX.1
  Module.Finite.of_surjective (DirectSum.component ℚ ℕ (fun n => rationalHomology X n) n)
    fun x => ⟨DirectSum.lof ℚ ℕ _ n x, DirectSum.component.lof_self ..⟩

/-- The Euler characteristic of a point is `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem eulerCharacteristic_unit : eulerCharacteristic Unit = 1 := by
  have h0 : Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology Unit 0) = 1 := by
    have e : rationalHomology Unit 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of ℚ (⨁ _ : Unit, ℚ) :=
      singularHomologyFunctorZeroOfTotallyDisconnectedSpace (ModuleCat ℚ) (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)
        (TopCat.of Unit) ≪≫ ModuleCat.coprodIsoDirectSum _
    rw [e.toLinearEquiv.finrank_eq]
    simp
  have hn (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) : Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology Unit n) = 0 := by
    have : Subsingleton (rationalHomology Unit n) :=
      ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton.mp <|
        isZero_singularHomologyFunctor_of_totallyDisconnectedSpace (ModuleCat ℚ) n
          (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ) (TopCat.of Unit) hn
    exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
  rw [eulerCharacteristic, finsum_eq_single _ 0 fun n hn' => by simp [hn n hn'], h0]
  simp

/-- The identity map is a Serre fibration. -/
@[category API, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_id (B : Type*) [TopologicalSpace B] :
    IsSerreFibration (ContinuousMap.id B) :=
  fun _ _ H hH => ⟨H, fun y => hH y, fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- The projection of a product onto one of its factors is a Serre fibration. -/
@[category API, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_fst (B F : Type*) [TopologicalSpace B] [TopologicalSpace F] :
    IsSerreFibration (ContinuousMap.fst : C(B × F, B)) :=
  fun _ f H hH =>
    ⟨H.prodMk (ContinuousMap.snd.comp (f.comp ContinuousMap.snd)),
      fun y => Prod.ext (hH y) rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩

/--
**Halperin conjecture.** Let $F \to E \xrightarrow{p} B$ be a (Serre) fibration of simply
connected spaces of finite rational type, with fibre $F = p^{-1}(b)$. If $F$ is rationally
elliptic with Euler characteristic $\chi(F) \neq 0$, then the rational cohomology Serre spectral
sequence of the fibration collapses at the $E_2$ page. Equivalently, the fibration is TNCZ: the
fibre inclusion $j \colon F \to E$ induces a surjection $H^*(E; \mathbb{Q}) \to H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$,
i.e. (dually, over the field $\mathbb{Q}$) an injection
$j_* \colon H_n(F; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(E; \mathbb{Q})$ in every degree $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 55]
theorem halperin_conjecture {E B : Type} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    [SimplyConnectedSpace E] [SimplyConnectedSpace B]
    (hE : IsFiniteRationalType E) (hB : IsFiniteRationalType B)
    (p : C(E, B)) (hp : IsSerreFibration p) (b : B) [SimplyConnectedSpace (p ⁻¹' {b})]
    (hF : IsRationallyElliptic (p ⁻¹' {b})) (hχ : eulerCharacteristic (p ⁻¹' {b}) ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (rationalHomologyMap (fibreInclusion p b) n).hom := by
  sorry

end

end HalperinConjecture

modeling_decisions: Conclusion: 'Serre spectral sequence collapses at E_2' is formalized as TNCZ (Lupton §1, citing McCleary Thm 5.9), and TNCZ (j^* : H^*(E;ℚ) → H^*(F;ℚ) surjective) is further rephrased as injectivity of j_* : H_n(F;ℚ) → H_n(E;ℚ) in every degree. Over the field ℚ, H^n(-;ℚ) is naturally the linear dual of H_n(-;ℚ) (universal coefficients) and a linear map between vector spaces is injective iff its transpose is surjective, so this is an exact equivalence with no finiteness needed. Mathlib has singular homology but neither singular cohomology nor spectral sequences.

Rational homology is Mathlib's `singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n` with coefficient object `ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ`; the chain complex is then ℚ[Sing_n X] (checked by `rfl` in a scratch file), i.e. genuine singular homology with ℚ coefficients. Because this coefficient object lives in `Type`, all spaces in the main statement are taken in `Type` (universe 0), as in other files of the collection (e.g. BingBorsuk).

'Fibration' is taken to mean Serre fibration (homotopy lifting property for all cubes I^n, n ≥ 0), the convention of Félix–Halperin–Thomas and the setting in which the Serre spectral sequence exists; this is the most general reading and implies the Hurewicz-fibration version. Bespoke `IsSerreFibration` defined on `C(E, B)`.

The fibre is F = p⁻¹(b) for a chosen point b : B (with the subspace topology); since B is simply connected (hence path connected) the choice of b is immaterial for a Serre fibration. Hypotheses on F (simply connected, rationally elliptic, χ ≠ 0) are imposed on this literal fibre.

Following Lupton's standing convention ('all spaces are simply connected ... of finite type over ℚ') and the decomposition notes, E and B are assumed of finite rational type (`IsFiniteRationalType`: each H_n(-;ℚ) finite-dimensional). The hypothesis on E is redundant (follows from B and F via the Serre spectral sequence) and F's is implied by ellipticity (proved as the API lemma `IsRationallyElliptic.isFiniteRationalType`); the conjecture is also believed equivalent without these (pullback from the finite-type classifying space Baut_1(F)), so they are harmless but a reviewer may prefer to drop them to match Wikipedia literally.

Spaces are arbitrary topological spaces rather than CW complexes; this is equivalent up to CW approximation since all invariants used are weak-homotopy invariants and a pullback of a Serre fibration along a weak equivalence of bases is a weak equivalence on total spaces with the same fibre.

`IsRationallyElliptic X` := the total rational homology ⨁_n H_n(X;ℚ) is a finite-dimensional ℚ-module, and for every basepoint x the total rational homotopy ⨁_{n≥0} ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive(π_{n+2}(X,x)) is finite-dimensional. Only π_n for n ≥ 2 is used, which is correct for simply connected X (π_1 = 0, π_0 a point); the definition is only meant for simply connected spaces, as documented. Quantifying over all basepoints is equivalent to a single one for path-connected X.

`eulerCharacteristic X` := ∑ᶠ n, (-1)^n · finrank_ℚ H_n(X;ℚ) : ℤ, using homology Betti numbers (equal to cohomology Betti numbers over ℚ). It is the true Euler characteristic whenever total rational homology is finite-dimensional, which is guaranteed by the ellipticity hypothesis on F; elsewhere it is a junk value (documented). Tested: `eulerCharacteristic Unit = 1`.
The hypothesis χ(F) ≠ 0 is taken literally as in Wikipedia (equivalent to χ(F) > 0 for elliptic F by Halperin's theorem, but the literal form is used).
The conclusion is stated for a universally quantified degree `n : ℕ` as a theorem parameter, i.e. injectivity in every degree, which is the full TNCZ condition.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Halperin conjecture

Let $F \to E \to B$ be a (Serre) fibration of simply connected spaces such that the fibre $F$ is
rationally elliptic (i.e. $\dim H_*(F; \mathbb{Q}) < \infty$ and
$\dim \pi_*(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} < \infty$) with non-zero Euler characteristic $\chi(F) \neq 0$.
The Halperin conjecture asserts that the rational cohomology Serre spectral sequence of the
fibration collapses at the $E_2$ page.

Collapse at $E_2$ is equivalent to the fibration being *totally non-cohomologous to zero* (TNCZ),
i.e. to the restriction $H^*(E; \mathbb{Q}) \to H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$ being surjective (see
[Lu97, §1]). Since rational cohomology is the linear dual of rational homology, this is in turn
equivalent to the fibre inclusion inducing an injection $H_*(F; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_*(E; \mathbb{Q})$
in every degree, which is the form in which the conjecture is stated below.

Note that a rationally elliptic space has non-negative Euler characteristic, so the hypothesis
$\chi(F) \neq 0$ is the same as $\chi(F) > 0$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Halperin conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halperin_conjecture)
- [Lu97] Lupton, G., *Variations on a conjecture of Halperin*, Homotopy and Geometry (Warsaw, 1997),
  Banach Center Publ. 45 (1998), 115–135. [arXiv:math/0010124](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0010124)
- [FHT93] Félix, Y., Halperin, S. and Thomas, J.-C., *Elliptic spaces II*, L'Enseignement
  Mathématique 39 (1993), 25–32.
-/

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicTopology Topology unitInterval

open scoped TensorProduct DirectSum

namespace HalperinConjecture

/-- A continuous map `p : E → B` is a *Serre fibration* if it has the homotopy lifting property
with respect to every cube $I^n$, $n \geq 0$: for every continuous `f : I^n → E` and every
homotopy `H : I × I^n → B` starting at `p ∘ f`, there is a homotopy `H' : I × I^n → E` lifting
`H` (that is `p ∘ H' = H`) and starting at `f`. -/
def IsSerreFibration {E B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] (p : C(E, B)) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : C(Fin n → I, E)) (H : C(I × (Fin n → I), B)), (∀ x, H (0, x) = p (f x)) →
    ∃ H' : C(I × (Fin n → I), E), (∀ y, p (H' y) = H y) ∧ ∀ x, H' (0, x) = f x

/-- The `n`-th singular homology group $H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological space `X` with
rational coefficients, as an object of `ModuleCat ℚ`. -/
noncomputable def rationalHomology (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) : ModuleCat ℚ :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).obj (TopCat.of X)

/-- The map $H_n(X; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(Y; \mathbb{Q})$ induced by a continuous map `f : X → Y`. -/
noncomputable def rationalHomologyMap {X Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    (f : C(X, Y)) (n : ℕ) : rationalHomology X n ⟶ rationalHomology Y n :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).map (TopCat.ofHom f)

/-- A topological space `X` is *rationally elliptic* if it is simply connected, its total
rational homology $H_*(X; \mathbb{Q}) = \bigoplus_n H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ is finite-dimensional,
and its total rational homotopy
$\pi_*(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = \bigoplus_n \pi_n(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ is finite-dimensional.
Since `X` is simply connected, $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ are trivial, so it suffices to consider the
(abelian) homotopy groups $\pi_{n+2}(X, x)$ for `n : ℕ`. -/
structure IsRationallyElliptic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  simplyConnected : SimplyConnectedSpace X
  finite_rationalHomology : Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n, rationalHomology X n)
  finite_rationalHomotopy : ∀ x : X, Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n : ℕ, ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive (π_ (n + 2) X x))

/-- The (rational) Euler characteristic
$\chi(X) = \sum_n (-1)^n \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological space `X`.
The sum is a `finsum`, so it is the usual Euler characteristic whenever only finitely many
rational homology groups are non-zero (e.g. for a rationally elliptic space). -/
noncomputable def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ n : ℕ, (-1) ^ n * (Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology X n) : ℤ)

/-- **Halperin conjecture.** Let $F \to E \xrightarrow{p} B$ be a (Serre) fibration of simply
connected spaces, where $F = p^{-1}(b)$ is the fibre over a point $b \in B$. Suppose that $F$ is
rationally elliptic (this includes $F$ being simply connected) and that $\chi(F) \neq 0$. Then
the rational cohomology Serre spectral sequence of the fibration collapses at the $E_2$ page.
Equivalently, the fibration is TNCZ: $H^*(E; \mathbb{Q}) \to H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$ is surjective,
or dually, the fibre inclusion $F \hookrightarrow E$ is injective on rational homology
$H_n(F; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(E; \mathbb{Q})$ in every degree $n$, which is the form stated here. -/
@[category research open, AMS 55]
theorem halperin_conjecture {E B : Type} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    [SimplyConnectedSpace E] [SimplyConnectedSpace B] (p : C(E, B)) (hp : IsSerreFibration p)
    (b : B) (hF : IsRationallyElliptic (p ⁻¹' {b})) (hχ : eulerCharacteristic (p ⁻¹' {b}) ≠ 0)
    (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective
      (rationalHomologyMap (⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩ : C(p ⁻¹' {b}, E)) n).hom := by
  sorry

/-- The identity map is a Serre fibration. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_id (E : Type*) [TopologicalSpace E] :
    IsSerreFibration (ContinuousMap.id E) := by
  intro n f H hH
  exact ⟨H, fun _ => rfl, fun x => hH x⟩

/-- The projection of a product onto a factor is a Serre fibration. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_snd (F B : Type*) [TopologicalSpace F] [TopologicalSpace B] :
    IsSerreFibration (ContinuousMap.snd : C(F × B, B)) := by
  intro n f H hH
  refine ⟨⟨fun y => ((f y.2).1, H y), by fun_prop⟩, fun _ => rfl, fun x => ?_⟩
  ext
  · rfl
  · exact hH x

end HalperinConjecture

abbrev RationalHomology (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Type :=

/-- A space is of finite rational type if its rational homology is finite-dimensional in every

def IsOfFiniteRationalType (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∀ n, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomology n X)

/-- The rationalized homotopy group `π_(n+2)(X, x) ⊗ ℚ`. The shift omits `π_0` and `π_1`, which
are trivial for the simply connected spaces in the conjecture. -/
abbrev RationalHomotopyGroup (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) : Type :=
  ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive (HomotopyGroup.Pi (n + 2) X x)

/-- The rational homology of `X` has finite total dimension. -/
def HasFiniteTotalRationalHomology (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∃ N, (∀ n, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomology n X)) ∧
    ∀ n, N < n → Subsingleton (RationalHomology n X)

/-- The higher rational homotopy groups of `X`, at `x`, have finite total dimension. -/
def HasFiniteTotalRationalHomotopy (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) : Prop :=
  ∃ N, (∀ n, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomotopyGroup n X x)) ∧
    ∀ n, N < n → Subsingleton (RationalHomotopyGroup n X x)

/-- A simply connected space is rationally elliptic when both its rational homology and its
rational homotopy have finite total dimension. Since the spaces used below are simply connected,
the choice of base point does not affect this condition. -/
def IsRationallyElliptic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  HasFiniteTotalRationalHomology X ∧ ∃ x, HasFiniteTotalRationalHomotopy X x

/-- The rational Euler characteristic, computed through degree `N`. -/
def rationalEulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (N : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1),
    (-1 : ℤ) ^ n * Module.finrank ℚ (RationalHomology n X)

/-- A space of finite total rational homology has nonzero Euler characteristic if an eventual
vanishing bound gives a nonzero alternating sum of rational Betti numbers. -/
def HasNonzeroEulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∃ N, (∀ n, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomology n X)) ∧

    rationalEulerCharacteristic X N ≠ 0

fibration of simply connected spaces collapses at the $E_2$ page when the fibre is rationally

- [Lupton, *Variations on a conjecture of Halperin*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0010124)

abbrev RationalHomology (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Type :=
  ((AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj
    (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).obj (TopCat.of X)

  ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩, ⟨1, by omega⟩, by simp⟩

/-- The rationalization of the homotopy group of `X` in degree `n + 2`.

The shift avoids dimensions zero and one. These are irrelevant to rational ellipticity here
because every space to which the definition is applied in the conjecture is simply connected. -/
abbrev RationalHigherHomotopy (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) : Type :=
  ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive (HomotopyGroup.Pi n.succ.succ X x)

/-- A space is of finite rational type if its rational homology in every degree is
finite-dimensional. -/
def IsFiniteRationalType (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomology n X)

/-- A pointed simply connected space is rationally elliptic if its total rational homology and
its total rational homotopy are finite-dimensional. The two bounds express that only finitely
many degrees are nonzero; degreewise finiteness expresses finite-dimensionality in each degree. -/
def IsRationallyElliptic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) : Prop :=
  (∃ N : ℕ,
    (∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomology n X)) ∧
    (∀ n > N, Subsingleton (RationalHomology n X))) ∧
  (∃ N : ℕ,
    (∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHigherHomotopy n X x)) ∧
    (∀ n > N, Subsingleton (RationalHigherHomotopy n X x)))

/-- The rational Euler characteristic of a space. On a rationally elliptic space this is the
finite alternating sum of the dimensions of its rational homology groups. -/
def rationalEulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ n : ℕ, if Even n then (Module.finrank ℚ (RationalHomology n X) : ℤ)
    else -(Module.finrank ℚ (RationalHomology n X) : ℤ)

/-- A map is a Serre fibration if it has the homotopy lifting property with respect to every
finite cube. This is the standard cubical characterization of Serre fibrations. -/
def IsSerreFibration {E B : Type} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    (p : C(E, B)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (g : C((Fin n → I), E)) (H : C(I × (Fin n → I), B)),
    (∀ a, p (g a) = H (0, a)) →
      ∃ G : C(I × (Fin n → I), E),

  ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩

def IsTNCZ {E B : Type} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    (p : C(E, B)) (b : B) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Injective
    (((AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj
      (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).map (TopCat.ofHom (fibreInclusion p b)))

spaces of finite rational type. If the fibre $F$ is rationally elliptic and has nonzero Euler
characteristic, then its rational-cohomology Serre spectral sequence collapses at the $E_2$

$H^*(E;\mathbb Q) \to H^*(F;\mathbb Q)$ is surjective. -/

    (E B : Type) [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    [SimplyConnectedSpace E] [SimplyConnectedSpace B]
    (p : C(E, B)) (b : B)
    [SimplyConnectedSpace {e : E // p e = b}]
    (x : {e : E // p e = b})
    (hp : IsSerreFibration p)
    (hE : IsFiniteRationalType E) (hB : IsFiniteRationalType B)
    (hF : IsRationallyElliptic {e : E // p e = b} x)
    (hχ : rationalEulerCharacteristic {e : E // p e = b} ≠ 0) :
    IsTNCZ p b := by

end

end HalperinConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Halperin conjecture

Let $F \to E \to B$ be a fibration of simply connected spaces such that the fibre $F$ is
*rationally elliptic* (both $H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$ and $\pi_*(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ are
finite-dimensional) and has non-zero Euler characteristic $\chi(F) \neq 0$. The Halperin
conjecture asserts that the (rational cohomology) Serre spectral sequence of the fibration
collapses at the $E_2$ page.

Since Mathlib has no Serre spectral sequence, we use the standard equivalent formulation
(see [Lupton, §1] and McCleary, *A User's Guide to Spectral Sequences*, Thm. 5.9): the Serre
spectral sequence collapses at $E_2$ if and only if the fibration is *totally non-cohomologous to
zero* (TNCZ), i.e. the fibre inclusion $j : F \to E$ induces a surjection
$j^* : H^*(E; \mathbb{Q}) \to H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$. Since $\mathbb{Q}$ is a field,
$H^n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ is naturally the dual of $H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$, so $j^*$ is surjective in
every degree if and only if $j_* : H_n(F; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(E; \mathbb{Q})$ is injective in
every degree. We state the conjecture in this last form, using Mathlib's singular homology with
rational coefficients.

Here "fibration" means Serre fibration (homotopy lifting property with respect to all cubes),
and the fibre is $F = p^{-1}(b)$ for a point $b$ of the base. Since $B$ is path connected, all
fibres are weakly homotopy equivalent, so the choice of $b$ does not matter.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Halperin conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halperin_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Topology)
- [Lupton, G., *Variations on a conjecture of Halperin*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0010124),
  Homotopy and Geometry (Warsaw, 1997), Banach Center Publ. 45 (1998), 115–135.
- Félix, Y., Halperin, S., Thomas, J.-C., *Rational Homotopy Theory*, GTM 205, Springer (2001).
-/

namespace HalperinConjecture

open AlgebraicTopology CategoryTheory DirectSum Topology TensorProduct
open scoped unitInterval

universe u

variable {E B : Type u} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]

/-- A continuous map `p : E → B` is a *Serre fibration* if it has the homotopy lifting property
with respect to every cube `I^n`: for every `f : I^n → E` and every homotopy `H : I × I^n → B`
starting at `p ∘ f`, there is a homotopy `H' : I × I^n → E` starting at `f` with
`p ∘ H' = H`. -/
def IsSerreFibration (p : C(E, B)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : C(I^Fin n, E)) (H : C(I × I^Fin n, B)),
    (∀ y, H (0, y) = p (f y)) →
      ∃ H' : C(I × I^Fin n, E), (∀ z, p (H' z) = H z) ∧ ∀ y, H' (0, y) = f y

/-- The identity map is a Serre fibration. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_id : IsSerreFibration (ContinuousMap.id E) :=
  fun _ _ H hH => ⟨H, fun _ => rfl, fun y => hH y⟩

/-- Any continuous map to a subsingleton (e.g. a one-point space) is a Serre fibration. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton B] (p : C(E, B)) : IsSerreFibration p :=
  fun _ f _ _ =>
    ⟨f.comp ⟨Prod.snd, continuous_snd⟩, fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- The inclusion `j : p⁻¹(b) → E` of the fibre of `p : E → B` over `b : B` into the total
space. -/
def fibreInclusion (p : C(E, B)) (b : B) : C(p ⁻¹' {b}, E) :=
  ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩

/-- The `n`-th singular homology functor with rational coefficients, `X ↦ H_n(X; ℚ)`, as a
functor from topological spaces to `ℚ`-vector spaces. (The coefficient module `ULift ℚ` is just
`ℚ` lifted to the universe of the spaces.) -/
noncomputable abbrev rationalHomologyFunctor (n : ℕ) : TopCat.{u} ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} ℚ :=
  (singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ (ULift.{u} ℚ))

/-- The `n`-th singular homology `H_n(X; ℚ)` of a topological space `X` with rational
coefficients, as a `ℚ`-vector space. -/
noncomputable abbrev rationalHomology (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) :
    ModuleCat.{u} ℚ :=
  (rationalHomologyFunctor n).obj (TopCat.of X)

/-- The (rational) Euler characteristic
$\chi(X) = \sum_i (-1)^i \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_i(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological space `X`.
This is only meaningful when the total rational homology of `X` is finite-dimensional, which
is guaranteed for rationally elliptic spaces; otherwise the sum is a `finsum` over an infinite
support and is `0` by convention. -/
noncomputable def rationalEulerChar (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ n : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ n * Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology X n)

/-- A topological space `X` is *rationally elliptic* if its total rational homology
$H_*(X; \mathbb{Q}) = \bigoplus_n H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ and its total rational homotopy
$\pi_*(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = \bigoplus_n \pi_n(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ are both
finite-dimensional over `ℚ`.

This definition is intended for simply connected spaces (for which `π_0` and `π_1` are trivial
and homotopy groups do not depend on the base point), so only the groups `π_n(X, x)` for
`n ≥ 2`, which are abelian, are tensored with `ℚ`. Since $\mathbb{Q}$ is a field,
$\dim H_*(X; \mathbb{Q}) < \infty$ is equivalent to $\dim H^*(X; \mathbb{Q}) < \infty$. -/
def IsRationallyElliptic (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n : ℕ, rationalHomology X n) ∧
    ∀ x : X, Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n : ℕ, ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive (π_ (n + 2) X x))

/-- **Halperin conjecture.** Let $F \to E \to B$ be a (Serre) fibration of simply connected spaces
such that the fibre $F$ is rationally elliptic and has non-zero Euler characteristic
$\chi(F) \neq 0$. Then the rational Serre spectral sequence of the fibration collapses at the
$E_2$ page.

Equivalently (see the module docstring), the fibration is totally non-cohomologous to zero: the
fibre inclusion $j : F \to E$ induces a surjection $H^*(E; \mathbb{Q}) \to H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$,
i.e. (dually) an injection $j_* : H_n(F; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(E; \mathbb{Q})$ for every `n`.

Here `p : E → B` is the fibration, `b : B` is any point of the base and `F = p ⁻¹' {b}` is the
fibre over `b`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 55]
theorem halperin_conjecture [SimplyConnectedSpace E] [SimplyConnectedSpace B]
    (p : C(E, B)) (hp : IsSerreFibration p) (b : B) [SimplyConnectedSpace (p ⁻¹' {b})]
    (hF : IsRationallyElliptic (p ⁻¹' {b})) (hχ : rationalEulerChar (p ⁻¹' {b}) ≠ 0)
    (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective
      ((rationalHomologyFunctor n).map (TopCat.ofHom (fibreInclusion p b))).hom := by
  sorry

end HalperinConjecture

The Halperin conjecture concerns the rational cohomology Serre spectral sequence of a fibration
whose fibre is rationally elliptic and has nonzero Euler characteristic.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Halperin conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halperin_conjecture)

open AlgebraicTopology CategoryTheory Topology
open scoped Cardinal Topology unitInterval

/-- Rational singular homology in degree `n`. -/
abbrev RationalHomology (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Type :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).obj (TopCat.of X)

/-- The map on rational singular homology induced by a continuous map. -/
abbrev rationalHomologyMap {X Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    (f : C(X, Y)) (n : ℕ) : RationalHomology n X →ₗ[ℚ] RationalHomology n Y :=
  (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).map
    (TopCat.ofHom f)).hom

/-- Rational cohomology, represented using the dual of rational singular homology. -/
abbrev RationalCohomology (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Type :=
  Module.Dual ℚ (RationalHomology n X)

/-- The contravariant map on rational cohomology induced by a continuous map. -/
abbrev rationalCohomologyMap {X Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    (f : C(X, Y)) (n : ℕ) : RationalCohomology n Y →ₗ[ℚ] RationalCohomology n X :=
  (rationalHomologyMap f n).dualMap

/-- A space is of finite rational type if its rational homology is finite-dimensional in every
 degree. -/
def IsOfFiniteRationalType (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomology n X)

/-- A map is a Serre fibration if it has the homotopy lifting property for every disk. -/
def IsSerreFibration {E B : Type} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    (p : C(E, B)) : Prop :=
  ∀ n (f : C(TopCat.disk.{0} n, E))
      (H : C(unitInterval × TopCat.disk.{0} n, B)),
    (∀ x, H (0, x) = p (f x)) →
      ∃ L : C(unitInterval × TopCat.disk.{0} n, E),
        (∀ x, L (0, x) = f x) ∧ ∀ z, p (L z) = H z

/-- A simply connected space is rationally elliptic if its total rational homology and total
rational homotopy are finite-dimensional. Since the fundamental group vanishes, the homotopy
condition starts in degree two. Integral ranks of the higher homotopy groups give their dimensions
after rationalization. -/
def IsRationallyElliptic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [SimplyConnectedSpace X] : Prop :=
  IsOfFiniteRationalType X ∧
    (∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n, N ≤ n → Subsingleton (RationalHomology n X)) ∧
    ∃ x : X, (∀ n : ℕ, Module.rank ℤ (Additive (π_ (n + 2) X x)) < Cardinal.aleph0) ∧
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n, N ≤ n → Module.rank ℤ (Additive (π_ (n + 2) X x)) = 0

/-- The rational Euler characteristic is nonzero. The cutoff exists because this predicate is
used for spaces whose total rational homology is finite-dimensional. -/
def HasNonzeroRationalEulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, (∀ n, N ≤ n → Subsingleton (RationalHomology n X)) ∧
    ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (-1 : ℤ) ^ n * (Module.finrank ℚ (RationalHomology n X) : ℤ) ≠ 0

rational type, and its fibre $F=p^{-1}(b)$ is rationally elliptic with nonzero Euler

    ∀ (E B : Type) [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
      (p : C(E, B)) (b : B)
      [SimplyConnectedSpace E] [SimplyConnectedSpace B]
      [SimplyConnectedSpace {e : E // p e = b}],
      IsOfFiniteRationalType E → IsOfFiniteRationalType B →
      IsSerreFibration p → IsRationallyElliptic {e : E // p e = b} →
      HasNonzeroRationalEulerCharacteristic {e : E // p e = b} →
      ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective
        (rationalCohomologyMap

/-- The `n`-th singular homology of `X` with rational coefficients. -/
noncomputable abbrev RationalHomology (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).obj (TopCat.of X)

degree. -/
def IsFiniteRationalType (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∀ n, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomology X n)

/-- The rationalization of the `(n + 2)`-nd homotopy group of `X` at `x`. -/
abbrev RationalHomotopy (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) (n : ℕ) :=
  TensorProduct ℤ ℚ (Additive (π_ (n + 2) X x))

/-- A space is rationally elliptic when its total rational homology and its total rational
homotopy have finite dimension. The homotopy groups are indexed from degree two; degree zero is
irrelevant for connected spaces, and degree one vanishes for simply connected spaces. -/
def IsRationallyElliptic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) : Prop :=
  (∀ n, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomology X n)) ∧
    {n | Nontrivial (RationalHomology X n)}.Finite ∧
  (∀ n, Module.Finite ℚ (RationalHomotopy X x n)) ∧
    {n | Nontrivial (RationalHomotopy X x n)}.Finite

/-- The Euler characteristic computed from rational singular homology. -/
noncomputable def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ n : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ n * (Module.finrank ℚ (RationalHomology X n) : ℤ)

/-- A continuous map is a Serre fibration if it has the homotopy lifting property with respect
to every finite-dimensional disk. -/
def IsSerreFibration {E B : Type} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    (p : C(E, B)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (g : C(TopCat.disk.{0} n, E)) (H : C(TopCat.disk.{0} n × unitInterval, B)),
    (∀ x, H (x, 0) = p (g x)) →
      ∃ G : C(TopCat.disk.{0} n × unitInterval, E),
        (∀ x, G (x, 0) = g x) ∧ ∀ z, p (G z) = H z

total space to the fibre is onto in rational cohomology. Equivalently, as expressed here, the
fibre inclusion is injective on rational homology in every degree. -/

    (p : C(E, B)) (b : B) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, Function.Injective
    (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).map
      (TopCat.ofHom ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩) :
        RationalHomology (Fiber p b) n ⟶ RationalHomology E n)

$E_2$; equivalently, the fibration is TNCZ.
-/

      IsSerreFibration p → IsRationallyElliptic (Fiber p b) x →
      eulerCharacteristic (Fiber p b) ≠ 0 → IsTNCZ p b := by
  sorry
